# Herzog–Schönheim conjecture

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«274»`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
- [arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
- [arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
- [PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
- [arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
-/

reformulations.difference: The imported canonical theorem adds `1 < ENat.card G` and does not explicitly require the subgroups to have finite index, whereas the cited papers explicitly discuss finite-index subgroups.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both hypotheses follow from the partition assumptions. Neumann's coset-cover lemma says that the finite-index cosets alone still cover the group; disjointness and nonemptiness therefore force every part to have finite index. Also, the representatives of distinct parts are distinct, so more than one part forces a nontrivial group, equivalently `1 < ENat.card G`. The scratch file proves these facts and the corresponding hypothesis-formulation equivalence for an arbitrary partition with more than one part.
